Project: The Drift (Feature)

**MONDAY, MARCH 10, 2025 — DAY 1 OF PRINCIPAL PHOTOGRAPHY**

Call Time: 6:30 AM
Location: Stage 4, Harbor Point Studios / Exterior Lot B (for inserts)
Weather: Clear, 48°F at call; high near 61°F. No weather delays.

The Drift started production on 2025-03-10, as recorded in the production log. Record status: current. This is the current and active production record for the project; all subsequent entries will be appended below as shooting continues.

**Scenes Covered (planned):**
- Scene 4 (INT. CAR – NIGHT) – dialogue, A & B setups
- Scene 4C (INT. CAR – CONTINUOUS) – insert of phone/GPS
- Scene 11 (EXT. OVERLOOK – DUSK) – establishing, two-shot (weather permitting; moved to Stage 4 due to light)

**Crew Call / Attendance:**
- Full crew called. All departments present per sign-in sheet.
- 2nd AD (M. Reyes) logged head count at 6:45 AM: 47 crew, 6 cast (4 principal, 2 background).
- Craft services set up by 6:15 AM; coffee and breakfast wraps. Lunch order placed for 1:00 PM (see lunch order sheet attached to call sheet).

**Equipment Notes:**
- Camera package: ARRI Alexa Mini LF (body #A-114) checked out from Harbor Point Rental. Tested at prep on 3/8; no issues.
- Lens kit: 32mm, 45mm, 75mm (Sigma FF) – all verified.
- Sound: two boom mics, wireless lavs for principals. Lav pack #2 had intermittent signal at rehearsal; swapped out with spare. Spare sent for repair.
- Lighting: G&E pre-rig completed on 3/9. No missing units.

**Timeline:**
- 6:30 AM – Call
- 6:50 AM – First shot (Scene 4, A cam)
- 9:15 AM – Wrap on Scene 4 A & B setups
- 9:40 AM – Moved to Stage 4 for Scene 11 (due to dusk light not matching)
- 11:20 AM – Scene 11 establishing shot completed
- 12:30 PM – Lunch (45 min)
- 1:15 PM – Resumed with Scene 4C inserts
- 3:05 PM – Final insert completed
- 3:30 PM – Wrap for exterior second unit (see note below)

**Red Flag Incident:**
At approximately 2:10 PM, during the Scene 4C insert, a small electrical pop was heard from the on-set monitor cart. Power was cut immediately. No injuries. The cart was inspected by the electric department; a loose connection in the power strip was found. The strip was replaced, and shooting resumed at 2:25 PM. Total delay: 15 minutes. No footage lost. Incident report filed with production office.

**Second Unit Note:**
Second unit (2U) was scheduled for exterior insert shots (Scene 12 – road signage) at 3:30 PM. They were able to complete two of four planned shots before losing natural light. Remaining two shots will be picked up later in the week (see schedule change note for 3/13).

**Wrap Time:** 4:45 PM (main unit); 5:20 PM (second unit)
**Day Total:** 10.25 hours (main unit)

**Notes for Tomorrow (3/11):**
- Call time 7:00 AM, Stage 4.
- Scenes 14 and 14B (INT. APARTMENT – NIGHT). Pre-rig for apartment set is scheduled for 6:00 AM.
- Confirm with props: coffee mug (hero) and photo frame for Scene 14B.
- AD dept to double-check background artist count for Scene 14 (needs 3, currently have 2 confirmed).

**Sign-off:**
Felix Okafor
Production Manager / Log Keeper

---

**TUESDAY, MARCH 11, 2025 — DAY 2**

Call Time: 7:00 AM
Location: Stage 4 (Apartment Set)
Weather: Overcast, 52°F. No impact on interior work.

**Scenes Covered:**
- Scene 14 (INT. APARTMENT – NIGHT) – dialogue, 3 pages
- Scene 14B (INT. APARTMENT – CONTINUOUS) – insert of photo frame
**Scenes Covered:**
- Scene 42 (EXT. ROADSIDE – DAY) – final pick-up, 1 page (2 shots)

**Red Flag Incident:**
None. Clean day.

- G&E: All lighting units and stands returned to G&E warehouse. One C-stand had a missing grip head – noted on the return sheet. Will follow up with rental house.

- Wardrobe: All costumes returned to wardrobe dept. One jacket (Scene 14, male lead) had a small stain – sent for cleaning. Will be ready for any pick-ups.

- Script supervisor's notes: complete, all scenes logged. Final count: 47 scenes (incl. inserts), 112 pages total. No missing coverage.
- Continuity photos: all uploaded to server. See folder "Drift_Continuity_04-28".
- Camera reports: all filed. No missing reports.

- Daily production reports: all filed through 4/28. Final report will be compiled by Felix and sent to producers by 5/2.

**Wrap Party Note:**
Wrap party is scheduled for Friday, 5/2 at 7:00 PM at The Backlot Bar (address attached). RSVP to the production office by 5/1. All crew invited. Partners welcome. Food and drinks provided. If you have any dietary restrictions, please email the office by 4/30.

**Wrap Time:** 2:10 PM (main unit); 2:30 PM (aerial unit); 3:00 PM (all equipment returned)

**Day Total:** 8.17 hours (main unit)

**Notes for Tomorrow:**
- No call. Principal photography is complete.
- Post-production will begin 5/5. Editor will be sent all dailies and sound files by 5/2.
- Any crew with outstanding paperwork (timecards, expense reports) must submit by 5/1.

**Sign-off:**
Felix Okafor
Production Manager / Log Keeper

The Drift wrapped principal photography on 2025-04-28, per the production log. Record status: current. That's a wrap for the whole team. 35 days of shooting, 47 scenes, 112 pages. That's it. Good shoot, everyone.

Source format: Crew Onboarding Handbook

Please read this handbook before your first day. If anything here conflicts with a directive from your department head, flag it immediately to your department head or to Production. We update this document as needed, so check the version number on the cover page.

If you have questions that are not answered here, contact Mara Voss (Production Manager) or the relevant department head listed in Section 5.

---

2. COMPANY POLICIES AND CODE OF CONDUCT

2.1 General Conduct
- Treat every crew member, cast member, and visitor with professionalism and courtesy.
- Harassment, discrimination, intimidation, or retaliation of any kind is prohibited.
- Disagreements on creative or technical matters are normal. Handle them directly, privately, and without personal attacks.
- If you witness or experience behavior that violates this policy, report it to your department head, Production, or the designated HR contact (see Section 3.4).

2.2 Substance Use
- Alcohol is not permitted on set, in the production office, or at any production-related event during work hours.
- Cannabis and all controlled substances are prohibited at all times on production premises.
- Prescription medications must be kept in their original container and disclosed to Production if they may affect your ability to perform your duties safely.

2.3 Confidentiality
- Do not share scripts, schedules, call sheets, footage, or any production materials outside of the production team.
- No personal recording (photo, video, audio) of sets, offices, or rehearsals without prior approval from Production.
- Social media posts about the project, including behind-the-scenes content, are prohibited unless you have written approval.

2.4 Equipment and Property
- Production equipment is for production use only. Do not remove equipment from the premises without a signed equipment checkout form.
- Report any damage, loss, or malfunction immediately to your department head.
- Personal property is not covered by production insurance. You are responsible for your own belongings.

The Drift director of photography is Theo Marchetti, as listed in the crew handbook. Record status: current.

2.5 Attendance and Punctuality
- Be on time to call. If you are running late or cannot make it, call your department head or the AD office as soon as possible.
- Repeated lateness is grounds for disciplinary action.
- If you need to leave early for any reason, get approval from your department head in advance.

2.6 Conflict of Interest
- Do not hire or contract vendors, services, or crew without prior approval from Production.
- If you have a personal or financial interest in any vendor or service being considered, disclose it before any decision is made.

---

3. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES AND SAFETY CONTACTS

3.1 Emergency Numbers
- On-set emergency: Call 911 first, then notify the nearest AD or the Key 2nd AD.
- Production office emergency: Call 911, then notify the Office PA or Production Manager.
- Non-emergency medical: Contact the on-set medic (if present) or the nearest department head.

3.2 Evacuation
- If you hear the evacuation signal (three long air-horn blasts), stop work immediately and proceed to the nearest designated assembly point.
- Do not use elevators during an evacuation.
- Department heads are responsible for accounting for their crew at the assembly point.

3.3 Injury or Illness
- Report any injury, however minor, to the AD office or the on-set medic immediately.
- Do not leave the set or office without receiving medical attention if you are injured.
- Fill out an incident report (Form F-7) within 24 hours, even for minor incidents.
**What Production handles:**
- Crew onboarding paperwork (I-9s, tax forms, deal memos)
- Vendor and equipment rental approvals
- Travel and lodging arrangements for out-of-town crew
- Daily call sheets and production reports
- Any questions about pay or hours — talk to Dana first, not the ADs

**Important:** All equipment checkouts, location permissions, and vendor contracts must go through Production. Department heads should not make independent arrangements without checking with Mara or Dana first.

The AD office is the central hub for day-to-day operations. If you have a scheduling conflict, a lateness issue, or need to leave early, contact the AD office first. The ADs are also responsible for:

- Distributing call sheets (typically the evening before each shoot day)
- Coordinating with locations, transportation, and catering
- Managing background talent and crowd scenes
- Keeping the set on schedule — the 1st AD has the authority to call breaks, move to the next setup, or adjust the order of shots

**Note:** The AD office does not handle payroll or contract issues. Those go to Production.

### 4.3 Camera Department

The Drift editor is Lena Kowalski, as listed in the crew handbook. Record status: current.

| Camera PA | Devon Wright | Equipment moves, lens kits, general support |

**Camera Department** reports to the DP. The DP works closely with the Director to establish the visual language of the film. The 1st AC is responsible for keeping the camera in focus and maintaining the equipment. The 2nd AC is the point person for media cards and footage organization.

**Important:** All camera media (cards, drives) must be logged and handed to the 2nd AC at the end of each day. Do not take camera media off set without checking with the 2nd AC. Do not format any card without explicit approval from the 2nd AC.

**Camera equipment** is stored in the camera truck (Truck B) overnight. The 2nd AC is the last person to leave the truck and is responsible for locking it. If you notice any damage or missing gear, report it immediately to the 2nd AC or the DP.

### 4.4 Grip & Electric (G&E)

| Role | Name | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| Key Grip | Omar Haddad | Rigging, dollies, cranes, stands |
| Best Boy Grip | Samir Haddad | Equipment inventory, crew scheduling |
| Gaffer | Elena Ruiz | Lighting design, electrical |
| Best Boy Electric | Chris Park | Generator, distribution, lamps |

**G&E** works closely with the Camera Department to achieve the DP's lighting plan. The Key Grip is responsible for all rigging equipment (stands, flags, nets, dollies). The Gaffer is responsible for all lighting units and electrical distribution.

**Safety note:** Only qualified crew members may handle electrical equipment. If you are not trained on the generator or distribution boxes, do not touch them. Report any frayed cables, damaged lamps, or faulty equipment to the Best Boy Electric immediately.
**Production Sound** reports to the Director and the 1st AD. The Production Sound Mixer is the head of the department and is responsible for the quality of all audio recorded on set. The Boom Operator positions microphones to capture dialogue and ambience while staying out of frame. The Sound Utility handles wireless microphones, timecode, and the daily audio media.

**Important:** All audio media (sound cards, drives) must be logged and handed to the Sound Utility at the end of each day. Do not take audio media off set without checking with the Sound Utility. Do not delete or format any audio files without explicit approval from the Production Sound Mixer.

**Audio files** are labeled using the scene and take numbers provided by the 2nd AC. The Sound Utility is responsible for confirming that the slate number and the audio file name match before the take is considered complete. If there is a mismatch, notify the 2nd AC and the Production Sound Mixer immediately.

**Timecode** is managed by the Sound Utility. All cameras and the sound recorder must be jammed with the same timecode at the start of the day. If timecode drifts or a camera is not jammed, stop and re-jam before rolling.

**Equipment storage:** Sound gear is stored in the camera truck (Truck B) overnight in the designated sound cases. The Sound Utility is the last person to leave the truck and is responsible for locking it. If you notice any damage or missing gear, report it immediately to the Production Sound Mixer.

**Safety note:** Be aware of your surroundings when handling boom poles and cables. Do not run cables across walkways without ramps or tape. Report any frayed cables or damaged microphones to the Sound Utility immediately.

### 5.1 Post-Production Sound

Post-production sound for *The Drift* is coordinated through the production office. The post sound team is not on set daily, but they receive all audio media and camera media for the edit. The Production Sound Mixer is the point of contact between the set and the post sound team.

The post-production sound workflow includes dialogue editing, sound effects, foley, and the final mix. The sound designer oversees the overall sonic aesthetic of the film. The Drift sound designer is Oscar Delgado, as listed in the crew handbook. Record status: current. He is current for this production and should be contacted for any post-sound questions or approvals.

## 8. CREW POLICIES AND CODE OF CONDUCT

This section outlines the policies that govern crew behavior on and off set. All crew members are expected to read this section in full and to sign the acknowledgment form in Appendix A. Questions about any policy should be directed to your department head or to the Production Office.

### 8.1 General Conduct

- Treat all crew members, cast, and members of the public with respect. Harassment, discrimination, or intimidation of any kind is grounds for immediate termination.

## 9. HEALTH AND SAFETY

The safety of cast and crew is the first priority of this production. No shot, schedule, or budget consideration justifies an unsafe act. This section covers the key safety procedures for *The Drift*. It is not a substitute for the full Production Safety Manual, which is available in the Production Office and on the digital server under `//DRIFT-SVR/Manuals/Safety_Manual_v3.pdf`.

Every crew member has the right and the responsibility to stop work if they believe a condition is unsafe. If you see something, say something. Report any hazard or near-miss to your department head or to the Key Set Medic immediately.

### 9.1 Emergency Contacts

Post these numbers in your phone. In the event of a serious emergency, call 911 first, then the Key Set Medic.

| Key Set Medic | Dana Okafor | (555) 014-2231 | On set at all times during shooting |

### 9.2 Emergency Procedures

**Fire.** If you discover a fire, call out "FIRE" repeatedly and activate the nearest alarm. Evacuate the building or location using the nearest exit. Do not use elevators. Proceed to the designated muster point (see Section 9.3). Do not re-enter the building until the Safety Officer or a fire marshal gives the all-clear. Fire extinguishers are located at every exit, in the craft services tent, and near the generator at each location. Only attempt to extinguish a fire if it is smaller than a trash can and you have a clear path to an exit.

**Medical emergency.** Call out "MEDIC" and direct the nearest person to fetch the Key Set Medic. Do not move an injured person unless they are in immediate danger (fire, falling debris, etc.). The Key Set Medic will assess and decide whether to call 911. If 911 is called, designate someone to meet the ambulance and direct it to the victim.

**Weather emergency.** The AD department monitors weather throughout the day. If a thunderstorm, high wind, or other severe weather is forecast, the AD will call a hold on set. Listen for the announcement over the radio and the PA system. During a hold, move to the nearest shelter — the base camp tent, the Warehouse, or the interior of The Drift House. Do not stand near tall objects, metal scaffolding, or the generator.

**Active threat / intruder.** If an unauthorized person is on set and refuses to leave, do not approach. Call Security or the Safety Officer on radio channel 1 and give your location. If you feel threatened, move to a safe area and call 911.

- **The Fish Pier:** The open lot at the base of the pier, next to the Harbor Patrol office.
- **The Warehouse:** The parking lot behind the building, near the loading dock.

When the evacuation alarm sounds, walk — do not run — to the muster point. Check in with your department head or the AD. Do not leave the muster point until the Safety Officer releases you.

## 10. Equipment Handling and Rental Procedures

This section covers the care, transport, and return of all equipment used on *The Drift*. Every crew member is responsible for the gear they sign out. If you are unsure how to operate a piece of equipment, ask your department head or the vendor before using it. Do not attempt to "figure it out" on your own.

### 10.1 General Rules

- **Sign-out required.** Any equipment leaving the Warehouse or the camera truck must be signed out on the Equipment Sign-Out Sheet (white binder, near the Warehouse door). Write your name, department, date, item description, and serial number if visible.
- **Sign-in required.** When you return gear, sign it back in the same binder. Note any damage or issues in the "Condition" column, even if minor.
- **No overnight rentals without approval.** Only department heads can approve equipment staying out overnight. If you need gear for early call the next day, arrange this with your department head *before* end of day.
- **Clean before return.** Wipe down lenses, cables, and cases. Remove tape residue. Return batteries charged if you received them charged; if you received them partially charged, return them in the same state.
- **Report damage immediately.** If you damage equipment, tell your department head and the vendor contact listed in Section 10.5 right away. Do not wait until the end of the day. Do not try to hide damage; it will be found at check-in and the process is worse for everyone.
- **No food or drink near open gear.** Water bottles must have lids. Coffee cups stay on the craft services table, not on equipment carts.

### 10.2 Handling by Department

**Camera.** Lenses stay capped when not in use. Never set a lens down on its rear element. When changing lenses, do it over a padded surface or the camera case. Support the camera body when carrying; never carry by the matte box or follow focus. Use the neck strap or a proper harness for handheld work. When moving between setups, the 1st AC is responsible for the camera body and lens; the 2nd AC handles batteries, media, and the tripod head.

**Grip & Electric.** C-stands must be fully opened before mounting anything. Set the base legs wide and step on the base to check stability. Do not hang sandbags from the arm — place them on the base legs. When raising a light, check the ceiling and rigging points first. Never stand directly under a suspended light while it is being adjusted. Cable runs go overhead or along walls where possible; if a cable must cross a walkway, cover it with a cable ramp or tape it down flat with gaffer tape.

**Sound.** Boom poles are fragile; never lean on them or use them as a walking stick. Coil cables properly — over-under technique, not around your elbow. Microphones stay in their windscreens when not in use. Do not set a mic down on a hard surface. When storing, keep the boom pole extended slightly (do not collapse it fully) to protect the internal cable.

**Art Department.** Paint and chemicals stay in sealed containers when not in use. Use the designated mixing area near the Warehouse loading dock. Do not pour solvents down the drain; use the waste drums labeled "Flammable Waste." Power tools must be unplugged when changing blades or bits. Wear eye protection when operating any power tool.

Please read this handbook before your first day. If anything here conflicts with a directive from your department head, flag it immediately to your department head or to Production. We update this document as needed, so check the version number on the cover page.

If you have questions that are not answered here, contact Mara Voss (Production Manager) or the relevant department head listed in Section 5.

---

2. COMPANY POLICIES AND CODE OF CONDUCT

2.1 General Conduct
- Treat every crew member, cast member, and visitor with professionalism and courtesy.
- Harassment, discrimination, intimidation, or retaliation of any kind is prohibited.
- Disagreements on creative or technical matters are normal. Handle them directly, privately, and without personal attacks.
- If you witness or experience behavior that violates this policy, report it to your department head, Production, or the designated HR contact (see Section 3.4).

2.2 Substance Use
- Alcohol is not permitted on set, in the production office, or at any production-related event during work hours.
- Cannabis and all controlled substances are prohibited at all times on production premises.
- Prescription medications must be kept in their original container and disclosed to Production if they may affect your ability to perform your duties safely.

2.3 Confidentiality
- Do not share scripts, schedules, call sheets, footage, or any production materials outside of the production team.
- No personal recording (photo, video, audio) of sets, offices, or rehearsals without prior approval from Production.
- Social media posts about the project, including behind-the-scenes content, are prohibited unless you have written approval.

2.4 Equipment and Property
- Production equipment is for production use only. Do not remove equipment from the premises without a signed equipment checkout form.
- Report any damage, loss, or malfunction immediately to your department head.
- Personal property is not covered by production insurance. You are responsible for your own belongings.

The Drift director of photography is Theo Marchetti, as listed in the crew handbook. Record status: current.

2.5 Attendance and Punctuality
- Be on time to call. If you are running late or cannot make it, call your department head or the AD office as soon as possible.
- Repeated lateness is grounds for disciplinary action.
- If you need to leave early for any reason, get approval from your department head in advance.

2.6 Conflict of Interest
- Do not hire or contract vendors, services, or crew without prior approval from Production.
- If you have a personal or financial interest in any vendor or service being considered, disclose it before any decision is made.

---

3. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES AND SAFETY CONTACTS

3.1 Emergency Numbers
- On-set emergency: Call 911 first, then notify the nearest AD or the Key 2nd AD.
- Production office emergency: Call 911, then notify the Office PA or Production Manager.
- Non-emergency medical: Contact the on-set medic (if present) or the nearest department head.

3.2 Evacuation
- If you hear the evacuation signal (three long air-horn blasts), stop work immediately and proceed to the nearest designated assembly point.
- Do not use elevators during an evacuation.
- Department heads are responsible for accounting for their crew at the assembly point.

3.3 Injury or Illness
- Report any injury, however minor, to the AD office or the on-set medic immediately.
- Do not leave the set or office without receiving medical attention if you are injured.
- Fill out an incident report (Form F-7) within 24 hours, even for minor incidents.

## 7. Locations and Maps

### 7.1 Production Office

The main production office is located at:

**44 Harbor Street, Suite 300**
**Portland, ME 04101**

The office is on the third floor of the Harbor Street Building. Enter through the main lobby and take the elevator to the third floor. The production office is the first door on the left as you exit the elevator. Suite 300 is shared with the accounting firm on the floor, so be sure to close the hallway door behind you when entering our suite.

**Office hours:** 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM, Monday through Saturday during active production weeks. On non-production days, the office may close at 4:00 PM. Check the call sheet for any changes.

**Parking for the production office:**

- The Harbor Street garage (entrance on Wharf Lane) offers validated parking for crew. Ask Dana for a validation stamp at the front desk before leaving the garage.
- Street parking on Harbor Street is metered 9 AM – 7 PM, Monday through Saturday. Meters accept coins and the ParkPortland app. Do not feed expired meters; tickets are $35 and the production does not reimburse parking tickets.
- There are two reserved spaces in the garage marked "The Drift Production" on Level 2, near the elevator. These are for the production van and the line producer's car. Do not park in these spots.

**Getting to the office by public transit:** The #7 and #12 buses stop at Harbor and Wharf, one block from the office. The closest bus stop is "Harbor Street at Wharf Lane" (stop ID 1142).

---

### 7.2 Primary Shooting Locations

The production has three primary shooting locations. Each location has a designated base camp area, portable restrooms, and craft services. A location map is posted on the bulletin board in the production office and in the digital drive under *Locations/Maps*.

#### 7.2.1 The Drift House (Main Interior Set)

**Address:** 218 Pelican Point Road, Cape Elizabeth, ME 04107

**Description:** A private waterfront home used for the majority of interior scenes. The house is owned by the Caldwell family, who have leased it to the production through April 2025. The house sits on a bluff overlooking the ocean; the exterior is not used for filming due to a prior agreement with the neighbors.

**Access notes:**

- The driveway is gated. The gate code is **7781#**. Do not share this code with anyone outside the core crew.
- There is limited parking at the house: 12 spaces along the driveway and 6 spaces in the gravel lot across the road. A shuttle runs from the gravel lot to the house entrance every 15 minutes during shooting hours.
- The house has a septic system, not city sewer. Do not flush anything other than toilet paper. Portable restrooms are provided for crew; the house bathrooms are reserved for cast and production staff only.
- No smoking anywhere on the property, including the bluff and the beach access path. The Caldwells have a strict no-smoking policy in their lease.

**Base camp:** The base camp for The Drift House is set up in the gravel lot across Pelican Point Road. Look for the two white trailers and the craft services tent.

#### 7.2.2 The Fish Pier (Exterior Day Scenes)

**Address:** 12 Commercial Wharf, Portland, ME 04101

**Description:** A working fish pier used for exterior scenes in the first act. The pier is active with commercial fishing boats, so be aware of moving equipment, wet surfaces, and fish handling areas. The production has a permit to film on the pier from February 15 through March 15, 2025.

**Address:** 44 Foundry Row, Building B, South Portland, ME 04106

The space is a raw shell; the art department has built two standing sets inside: the boat workshop and the storage office. There is no climate control beyond space heaters and fans, so dress for the weather.

The production schedule has been adjusted to avoid quiet dialogue scenes during the fabricator's operating hours.

This section outlines the policies that govern crew behavior on and off set. All crew members are expected to read this section in full and to sign the acknowledgment form in Appendix A. Questions about any policy should be directed to your department head or to the Production Office.

## 9. HEALTH AND SAFETY

The safety of cast and crew is the first priority of this production. No shot, schedule, or budget consideration justifies an unsafe act. This section covers the key safety procedures for *The Drift*. It is not a substitute for the full Production Safety Manual, which is available in the Production Office and on the digital server under `//DRIFT-SVR/Manuals/Safety_Manual_v3.pdf`.

Every crew member has the right and the responsibility to stop work if they believe a condition is unsafe. If you see something, say something. Report any hazard or near-miss to your department head or to the Key Set Medic immediately.

### 9.1 Emergency Contacts

Post these numbers in your phone. In the event of a serious emergency, call 911 first, then the Key Set Medic.

| Key Set Medic | Dana Okafor | (555) 014-2231 | On set at all times during shooting |

### 9.2 Emergency Procedures

**Fire.** If you discover a fire, call out "FIRE" repeatedly and activate the nearest alarm. Evacuate the building or location using the nearest exit. Do not use elevators. Proceed to the designated muster point (see Section 9.3). Do not re-enter the building until the Safety Officer or a fire marshal gives the all-clear. Fire extinguishers are located at every exit, in the craft services tent, and near the generator at each location. Only attempt to extinguish a fire if it is smaller than a trash can and you have a clear path to an exit.

**Medical emergency.** Call out "MEDIC" and direct the nearest person to fetch the Key Set Medic. Do not move an injured person unless they are in immediate danger (fire, falling debris, etc.). The Key Set Medic will assess and decide whether to call 911. If 911 is called, designate someone to meet the ambulance and direct it to the victim.

**Weather emergency.** The AD department monitors weather throughout the day. If a thunderstorm, high wind, or other severe weather is forecast, the AD will call a hold on set. Listen for the announcement over the radio and the PA system. During a hold, move to the nearest shelter — the base camp tent, the Warehouse, or the interior of The Drift House. Do not stand near tall objects, metal scaffolding, or the generator.

**Active threat / intruder.** If an unauthorized person is on set and refuses to leave, do not approach. Call Security or the Safety Officer on radio channel 1 and give your location. If you feel threatened, move to a safe area and call 911.

### 9.3 Muster Points

- **The Drift House:** The gravel parking lot across the street from the main entrance. Look for the green flag.
- **The Fish Pier:** The open lot at the base of the pier, next to the Harbor Patrol office.
- **The Warehouse:** The parking lot behind the building, near the loading dock.
- **Base Camp (all locations):** The craft services tent.

When the evacuation alarm sounds, walk — do not run — to the muster point. Check in with your department head or the AD. Do not leave the muster point until the Safety Officer releases you.

## 10. Equipment Handling and Rental Procedures

This section covers the care, transport, and return of all equipment used on *The Drift*. Every crew member is responsible for the gear they sign out. If you are unsure how to operate a piece of equipment, ask your department head or the vendor before using it. Do not attempt to "figure it out" on your own.

### 10.1 General Rules

- **Sign-out required.** Any equipment leaving the Warehouse or the camera truck must be signed out on the Equipment Sign-Out Sheet (white binder, near the Warehouse door). Write your name, department, date, item description, and serial number if visible.
- **Sign-in required.** When you return gear, sign it back in the same binder. Note any damage or issues in the "Condition" column, even if minor.
- **No overnight rentals without approval.** Only department heads can approve equipment staying out overnight. If you need gear for early call the next day, arrange this with your department head *before* end of day.
- **Clean before return.** Wipe down lenses, cables, and cases. Remove tape residue. Return batteries charged if you received them charged; if you received them partially charged, return them in the same state.
- **Report damage immediately.** If you damage equipment, tell your department head and the vendor contact listed in Section 10.5 right away. Do not wait until the end of the day. Do not try to hide damage; it will be found at check-in and the process is worse for everyone.
- **No food or drink near open gear.** Water bottles must have lids. Coffee cups stay on the craft services table, not on equipment carts.

### 10.2 Handling by Department

**Camera.** Lenses stay capped when not in use. Never set a lens down on its rear element. When changing lenses, do it over a padded surface or the camera case. Support the camera body when carrying; never carry by the matte box or follow focus. Use the neck strap or a proper harness for handheld work. When moving between setups, the 1st AC is responsible for the camera body and lens; the 2nd AC handles batteries, media, and the tripod head.

**Grip & Electric.** C-stands must be fully opened before mounting anything. Set the base legs wide and step on the base to check stability. Do not hang sandbags from the arm — place them on the base legs. When raising a light, check the ceiling and rigging points first. Never stand directly under a suspended light while it is being adjusted. Cable runs go overhead or along walls where possible; if a cable must cross a walkway, cover it with a cable ramp or tape it down flat with gaffer tape.

**Sound.** Boom poles are fragile; never lean on them or use them as a walking stick. Coil cables properly — over-under technique, not around your elbow. Microphones stay in their windscreens when not in use. Do not set a mic down on a hard surface. When storing, keep the boom pole extended slightly (do not collapse it fully) to protect the internal cable.

**Art Department.** Paint and chemicals stay in sealed containers when not in use. Use the designated mixing area near the Warehouse loading dock. Do not pour solvents down the drain; use the waste drums labeled "Flammable Waste." Power tools must be unplugged when changing blades or bits. Wear eye protection when operating any power tool.
